newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire up on bid, capped by trade update.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire up on bid, capped by trade update.

text.p: Shares in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc were slightly firmer on Wednesday as a sobering trading statement limited gains after a bid approach was revealed.
Granada Group Plc launched a 711 million stg ($1.2 billion) bid for the remaining 73 percent of Yorkshire it does not already own.
Yorkshire shares were up only 2-1/2p to 1157-1/2, having initially climbed as high as 1170p.
Granada said the offer of two new Granada shares and 1,825.32p in cash for every three Yorkshire shares valued Yorkshire ordinary shares at 1175p each, which was well within analysts' expectations.
Analysts said the terms of Granada's offer held no surprises.
"What's hurting the (Yorkshire) shares is its trading statement...It's a pretty damning indictment of what's happening," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
Yorkshire, in the statement, said it expected a disappointing second quarter, citing lower-than-expected growth in ITV advertising revenue and a failure to increase market share.

The statement also said the company believes total advertising revenue growing for ITV will show only minimal growth during the first half of 1997. It blamed the slowdown on the launch of a new channel and industry-wide weakness.
"They're giving the reasons why they caved into Granada and didn't hold out for a higher price," the analyst added.

Granada also was dragged down by a report in the Financial Times that said the Independent Television Commission faces possible legal and regulatory challenges to its decision to award licences for broadcasting digital terrestrial TV in the UK to the British Digital Broadcasting consortium, of which Granada is a part.
Shares in Carlton Communications Plc, also a member of the consortium, were down 2-1/2p to 522-1/2.
